name: Skin
func: The body's largest organ and outer barrier. It keeps germs and water loss out, controls body temperature with sweat and blood flow, senses touch, heat and pain, and makes vitamin D.

levels.kid:
Your **skin** is the biggest part of your body, and it covers you from head to toe, like a stretchy suit.

It **protects** you. It keeps germs out and keeps water in, so you do not dry up.

It helps you **feel** things: soft fur, a pinch, cold ice or a warm bath. When you are hot, it **sweats** to cool you down. When you get a cut, it **heals itself**.

Your skin is always making new cells and shedding old ones. Every day, tiny flakes of old skin fall off, too small to see. It also uses sunshine to make **vitamin D** for strong bones.
levels.hs:
The **skin** (integument) is the body's largest organ, covering about 1.5–2 m² in an adult and making up roughly 15% of body weight. It has three layers.

The **epidermis** is the thin outer layer, made mostly of **keratinocytes** that are born at the bottom and move up, filling with tough **keratin** and dying to form a waterproof surface layer. It also contains **melanocytes**, which make the pigment **melanin** that protects against UV light. The epidermis has no blood vessels.

The **dermis** lies beneath. It is thick connective tissue rich in **collagen** and **elastin**, with blood vessels, nerves, **hair follicles**, **sweat glands** and **sebaceous (oil) glands**. Its ridges create fingerprints.

The **hypodermis** (subcutaneous tissue) is mostly **fat**, which insulates, cushions and stores energy. Below it lie fascia and muscle.

Functions include **protection** (from germs, chemicals, UV and water loss), **temperature control** (sweating and widening or narrowing skin blood vessels), **sensation** (touch, pressure, vibration, heat, cold, pain and itch), and making **vitamin D** in sunlight. The skin also acts as an immune organ.
levels.college:
**Epidermal layers** (deep to superficial): **stratum basale** (a single layer of dividing stem cells attached to the basement membrane), **stratum spinosum** (cells joined by **desmosomes**), **stratum granulosum** (keratohyalin granules and lamellar bodies that release lipids), **stratum lucidum** (only in thick skin of palms and soles) and **stratum corneum** (flattened, dead corneocytes in a lipid matrix, the "bricks and mortar"). A keratinocyte takes roughly four weeks to travel from basale to shedding.

**Other epidermal cells:** **melanocytes** (from neural crest) transfer melanin in melanosomes to keratinocytes; skin colour reflects melanosome size, type and distribution, not melanocyte number. **Langerhans cells** are antigen-presenting immune cells, and **Merkel cells** are touch receptors.

**Dermis:** the **papillary dermis** (loose connective tissue in the dermal papillae, with capillary loops and **Meissner corpuscles**) and the deeper **reticular dermis** (dense irregular connective tissue). **Pacinian corpuscles** lie deeper, sensing vibration. **Langer's lines** follow collagen orientation, and incisions along them heal with less scarring.

**Glands:** **eccrine sweat glands** open directly onto the skin, everywhere, for cooling; **apocrine glands** in the armpits open into hair follicles; **sebaceous glands** release sebum into follicles.

**Nerve supply:** each spinal nerve supplies a band of skin, a **dermatome** (C6 thumb, T4 mid-chest, T10 umbilicus, L4 medial leg, S1 lateral foot).

**Blood supply:** two horizontal plexuses (superficial and deep) linked by vertical vessels. **Arteriovenous anastomoses** in fingers, toes and ears regulate heat loss.
levels.phd:
The **stratum corneum** barrier is a feat of biochemistry. Corneocytes are wrapped in a **cornified envelope** of cross-linked proteins (loricrin, involucrin) made by **transglutaminases**, and embedded in lipid lamellae of **ceramides**, cholesterol and free fatty acids in roughly equal molar ratios. Breakdown of **filaggrin** produces amino acids that form the skin's "natural moisturising factor". **Loss-of-function filaggrin mutations** are a major genetic risk factor for **atopic dermatitis**, supporting the "outside-in" barrier hypothesis of allergy.

**Epidermal stem cells** in the basal layer and **hair follicle bulge** (marked by **Lgr5**, **Krt15** and others) maintain the epidermis and contribute to wound repair. Basal cells exit the cell cycle under **Notch** signalling to differentiate. Wound healing proceeds through overlapping phases: haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation (re-epithelialisation, angiogenesis and fibroblast-driven matrix deposition, with **myofibroblasts** contracting the wound) and remodelling (type III collagen replaced by type I). Scar tissue reaches only about 70–80% of normal strength.

**Vitamin D synthesis:** UVB converts **7-dehydrocholesterol** in keratinocytes to **previtamin D3**, then vitamin D3, which is hydroxylated in the liver and kidney.

**Pigmentation:** UV damage triggers p53-driven expression of **POMC** in keratinocytes, which is cleaved to **α-MSH**; this binds the **MC1R** receptor on melanocytes, increasing eumelanin production, which is the tanning response. **MC1R variants** cause red hair and fair skin and increase melanoma risk.

**Immune function:** skin hosts resident memory T cells, dendritic cells and antimicrobial peptides such as **cathelicidins** and **β-defensins**. The **skin microbiome** (e.g., *Staphylococcus epidermidis*) shapes immune tolerance and pathogen defence.
levels.expert:
**Exam:** describe lesions systematically: type (**macule**, papule, plaque, vesicle, bulla, pustule, nodule), size, colour, distribution and arrangement. Use **dermoscopy** for pigmented lesions and the **ABCDE** rule for melanoma (Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Colour variation, Diameter over 6 mm, Evolving). **Nikolsky's sign** (skin shears off with light pressure) suggests pemphigus vulgaris or **toxic epidermal necrolysis**, a dermatological emergency. Skin turgor and capillary refill hint at hydration and perfusion.

**Burns** are classified by depth: superficial (epidermis), partial-thickness (into dermis; blisters, painful) and full-thickness (through dermis; leathery, painless because nerve endings are destroyed). Extent is estimated with the **Rule of Nines** or Lund–Browder chart. Major burns need fluid resuscitation, specialist care and often skin grafts.

**Skin cancers:** basal cell carcinoma (most common, pearly papule with telangiectasia, rarely spreads), squamous cell carcinoma (sun-exposed skin, can spread) and **melanoma** (most deadly; **Breslow thickness** predicts prognosis). Treatment ranges from excision (with **Mohs surgery** for delicate areas) to immunotherapy for advanced melanoma.

**Neurology and the skin:** **neurocutaneous syndromes** matter for neurosurgeons: **neurofibromatosis type 1** (café-au-lait macules, neurofibromas, axillary freckling), **tuberous sclerosis** (ash-leaf macules, facial angiofibromas, cortical tubers) and **Sturge–Weber syndrome** (port-wine stain in the trigeminal territory with leptomeningeal angioma). A **midline lumbar hair tuft, dimple or haemangioma** may signal occult **spinal dysraphism** (tethered cord).

**Dermatomal mapping** localises nerve root lesions; **shingles** (herpes zoster) follows a dermatome. **Pressure ulcers** are graded 1–4 and are prevented by turning and pressure relief.

Surgically, incisions follow **Langer's lines** and relaxed skin tension lines to minimise scarring.

keyPoints: Largest organ: epidermis, dermis and hypodermis
Epidermis = keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans and Merkel cells; no blood vessels
Barrier, temperature control, sensation, vitamin D, immunity
Dermatomes map skin to spinal nerves (T10 = umbilicus)
Neurocutaneous signs (café-au-lait, ash-leaf, port-wine stain) point to brain disease

test.q: Which layer of the skin has no blood vessels?
test.explain: The epidermis is avascular and fed by diffusion from the dermis.

test.q: The pigment made by melanocytes is ______.
test.explain: Melanin absorbs UV radiation and protects DNA in keratinocytes.

test.q: Which spinal dermatome is at the level of the umbilicus?
test.explain: T10 covers the belly button; T4 runs roughly at chest level.

test.q: Café-au-lait macules and neurofibromas suggest which condition?
test.explain: NF1 is a neurocutaneous syndrome with nerve sheath tumours.

test.q: Melanoma prognosis is best predicted by ______ thickness.
test.explain: Breslow thickness is measured in millimetres from the granular layer to the deepest tumour cells.

test.q: Why is a full-thickness burn often painless?
choices: Nerve endings in the dermis are destroyed
test.explain: Full-thickness burns destroy the dermis and its sensory receptors.
